sections.title: Background and Career
sections.content:

Before relocating to the U.S. Virgin Islands in 2003, she practiced at Solomon Blum Heymann LLP, a boutique Wall Street tax firm specializing in ultra-wealthy individuals and closely held corporations. In the USVI, she initially worked at the Law Offices of Marjorie Rawls Roberts P.C., a local firm specializing in EDC tax incentive programs and estate planning. She founded her own practice, Erika A. Kellerhals P.C., in 2008, and in 2011 co-founded Kellerhals Ferguson LLP with Greg Ferguson, a former colleague from the Roberts firm. The partnership evolved into Kellerhals Ferguson Kroblin PLLC with the addition of Christopher Kroblin, a litigator. Kellerhals holds bar admissions in New York (2001), the U.S. Virgin Islands, Florida, England & Wales, and the United States Tax Court. Her firm’s specialization in individual, corporate, partnership, and international taxation—combined with familiarity with the USVI’s Economic Development Commission program—aligned with the needs of Epstein’s offshore-domestic corporate structure. She also served on the board of the St. Thomas-St. John Chamber of Commerce. The firm maintains a New York office at 40 Wall Street, 35th Floor, and an affiliation with Solomon Blum Heymann LLP, with Kellerhals listed as Of Counsel at the New York firm.

sections.title: Key Relationships
sections.content:
Kellerhals’s primary professional relationship was with Jeffrey Epstein himself, documented across more than twenty emails spanning 2015 to 2019. Communications were frequently mediated through Lesley Groff, Epstein’s executive assistant, with subject lines reading “Jeffrey Epstein” or “Quick call with JEE.” The tone of direct exchanges between Kellerhals and Epstein extended beyond attorney-client formality. Two days after the 2016 presidential election, Kellerhals emailed Epstein: “But holy shit you were spot on about trump!” followed by “I am so sorry this happened to you. It is terrible. And sad.” Epstein responded: “its funny, dont lose your sense of humor” [HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_032348]. In November 2018, Epstein offered Kellerhals luxury Apple Watch bands through an intermediary: “Anything you want! Jeffrey says it is your gift and whatever you want you can have! (So nice! Including Hermes!)” [EFTA02264321].

Within the Epstein corporate hierarchy, Kellerhals worked alongside Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn, though with defined jurisdictional boundaries. Kellerhals and Indyke co-occur in 82 LMSBAND files and shared officer positions across Gratitude America Ltd, J. Epstein Virgin Islands Foundation, and Enhanced Education. However, Kahn confirmed in November 2018 that Kellerhals “does not have signing authority” on the brokerage account of the Epstein Virgin Islands Foundation, despite her Secretary and Treasurer titles [EFTA01373347]. This arrangement—named on corporate documents but excluded from transactional control—is consistent with Kellerhals handling local legal and regulatory matters while New York-based Indyke and Kahn retained financial authority.

Kellerhals also maintained a working relationship with Brett Geary, operator of Business Basics VI LLC, the registered agent entity that served more than twenty Epstein USVI entities. Both shared the same office address at 9053 Estate Thomas, Suite 101, and co-signed as incorporators on multiple Epstein entities beginning in November 2011 (Nautilus Inc, Maple Inc, Laurel Inc). The Kellerhals-Geary-BBVI relationship formed the organizational core of Epstein’s USVI corporate presence.

sections.title: USVI Corporate and Tax Work
sections.content:
Kellerhals’s earliest documented work for Epstein dates to June 2009, when she authored the FTC/EDC response to a determination letter regarding Epstein’s Industrial Development Certificate benefits (GRM Master Filing Index, page 6). The IDC program provided substantial tax advantages to qualifying USVI businesses, including reduced gross receipts tax and exemption from USVI income tax. Kellerhals managed these applications and compliance filings—work that went beyond registering corporate entities.

She advised Epstein on USVI residency requirements, informing him in August 2015 that 153 days in the territory would “still not be a resident” [EFTA02488622]. In June 2013, she advocated for dynasty trust legislation in the USVI—“We need dynasty trust legislation here in the USVI” [EFTA02370395]—a move that would have made the territory more favorable for long-term wealth structures. She researched residency for naturalization under INA Section 319(a) in September 2013 and later analyzed the tax implications of the 2017 “Chapo” tax law changes.

Kellerhals served as incorporator for Financial Strategy Group Ltd (later renamed Southern Country International Ltd), an entity organized to operate as an international banking entity under USVI Code Title 9, Chapter 25 [EFTA01265913]. The articles authorized 1,000,000 shares at $5.00 par value with a $500,000 minimum to commence operations. The international banking entity designation indicates that Epstein, through Kellerhals, sought to establish a licensed banking operation in the USVI, not merely a trust company or holding structure. A Certificate of Good Standing was issued under the new name Southern Country International Ltd on July 9, 2018.

sections.title: Political Connections and Government Relations
sections.content:
Documentary evidence establishes Kellerhals as Epstein’s primary contact with USVI political leadership. In February 2017, she emailed Epstein: “Would you be willing to meet with Albert Bryan? He is the former Commissioner of Labor who is running for Governor” [EFTA02366972]. In September 2018, during Bryan’s gubernatorial campaign, she arranged another meeting at Epstein’s Southern Trust Company offices on St. Thomas [EFTA02259117]. Bryan won the election on November 6, 2018. Eight days later, on November 14, Kellerhals emailed Epstein: “Meeting happening now re endorsement. Will call you after. Spoke to Stacey. She and I are good.” Later that afternoon: “I tried you. Deal is done. Need wire :)” [EFTA02616202]. The same-day sequence of an endorsement meeting, a reference to “Stacey” (likely USVI Delegate Stacey Plaskett), and a wire transfer request has not been publicly explained.

After Bryan’s inauguration in January 2019, Kellerhals hosted an Epstein-Bryan meeting at her law office on February 7, 2019—five months before Epstein’s arrest. The meeting was coordinated by Cecile de Jongh, former USVI First Lady and wife of former Governor John de Jongh [EFTA02274532]. According to RealClearInvestigations, Bryan subsequently requested the USVI Justice Department provide Epstein with a sex offender registry waiver. Kellerhals’s relationship with the de Jonghs was politically sensitive: in September 2015, she had warned Epstein regarding then-Governor Kenneth Mapp, “Definitely don’t mention Cecile and John. Honestly I wish I could say he wasn’t going to do something stupid or criminal but I can’t say that. He’s a wild card” [EFTA02486512]. Kellerhals also appeared on a direct email thread with Governor Mapp and Epstein simultaneously in July 2017, discussing invoicing for legal work her firm had performed for the USVI government [EFTA02343702].

FEC records document Kellerhals’s bipartisan political donation pattern: approximately $13,000 in federal contributions from 2009 to 2023, with the largest share ($7,632) directed to Stacey Plaskett’s campaigns via Virgin Islands for Plaskett and ActBlue. Other recipients included Beto O’Rourke ($2,700), the DCCC ($2,500), Mitch McConnell ($1,000), Charles Rangel ($1,000), and Maggie Hassan ($500). Darren Indyke and Lesley Groff also donated to Plaskett, a pattern noted in the record of Epstein-associated political giving to the USVI delegate. Kellerhals additionally donated $1,000 to Bryan’s territorial gubernatorial campaign, which does not appear in federal FEC data. She had no FARA registrations or LDA lobbying disclosures despite her documented meetings “on the Hill” in Washington, D.C. (EFTA02239485, March 2018).

sections.title: Financial Activity and Deutsche Bank
sections.content:
Kellerhals was paid directly by Epstein via checks drawn on Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas, issued from Jeffrey Epstein’s account at 6100 Red Hook Quarter B3, St. Thomas, USVI, and made payable to Kellerhals Ferguson [EFTA01292472]. Beyond legal fees, she negotiated real estate transactions on Epstein’s behalf. In September 2015, Epstein emailed her a detailed bid strategy for a St. Thomas property: “knowing da mour, I would first bid cash of 10 plus a note of 5. they will come back at 20. then we bid 10 cash plus a note of 6 they will agree I think to 10 cash and a note of 7-8, then we offer all cash of 15.” Kellerhals responded: “LOL — I woke thinking about this. Sounds like a plan” [EFTA02344089]. In October 2015, she reported on another transaction: “expecting contract shortly then the real fun begins” with “chris, my litigator, is waiting to review the contract” [EFTA02349311]. She also managed a Dutch-language property transaction that same month [EFTA02342425].

Deutsche Bank performed a formal KYC/compliance screening of Kellerhals on October 12, 2016 [EFTA01363310]. Her GCIS ID was 11593661; the OFAC check returned no match; LexisNexis found one public record; BIS screening found no negative, non-negative, or foreign-language media. The PCR case was auto-closed as no-hit. This screening placed Kellerhals in the same compliance review as Indyke and Kahn—the bank classified her as a related person for Epstein account management rather than as an independent outside professional. She also appeared on Deutsche Bank account-opening documents for the Butterfly entity in October 2018, listed alongside Indyke, Kahn, and the Bellers.

Despite holding Secretary and Treasurer titles for the Epstein Virgin Islands Foundation, Kellerhals had no signing authority on its brokerage account. Richard Kahn stated this in a November 2018 internal Deutsche Bank email: “please note that Erika Kellerhals who is secretary and treasurer does not have signing authority on this account” [EFTA01373347]. This arrangement—corporate titles without financial authority—placed Kellerhals in a regulatory-facing position for USVI entities while actual account control remained with the New York-based officers.

sections.title: Island Operations Management
sections.content:
Email evidence shows that Kellerhals managed Epstein’s day-to-day USVI operations beyond what her corporate attorney role would typically entail. She handled WAPA utility matters and island electricity for staff named Danny and Bryan (EFTA02471784, February 2016). She managed construction permitting, submitting architect letters and signed cistern permits for the island properties (EFTA02668260, December 2016). She oversaw staff transitions, including caretaker changes that required Epstein’s personal approval: “no i want a transition asap but i want to understand everything before change” (EFTA02476178, January 2016). She also managed the VIFFO LLC real estate entity, handling list price inquiries in December 2015 [EFTA02549898].

Calendar entries from Lesley Groff’s scheduling emails confirm regular in-person meetings between Kellerhals and Epstein at the Southern Trust Company offices on St. Thomas. On January 12, 2016, Kellerhals had a 1:00 PM meeting at STC the same day Epstein conducted a 3:30 PM conference call regarding Apollo Global Management’s Josh Black with Perry Lerner and Chris Calise [EFTA02362419]. Additional STC meetings are documented on March 27, 2018 [EFTA02240988] and June 5, 2019 [EFTA02290205]—the latter occurring one month before Epstein’s arrest. The documented frequency of these meetings increased in 2018–2019.

sections.title: The Will and Estate Proceedings
sections.content:
Kellerhals filed the only known affidavit attesting to the authenticity of Epstein’s will, which was signed on August 8, 2019—two days before his death at the Metropolitan Correctional Center. The will created “The 1953 Trust” (referencing Epstein’s birth year) to hold his estimated $577 million estate. In her affidavit, Kellerhals stated that she knew of no other will or codicil and that Epstein had personally sent her a copy before his death.

KFK PLLC was appointed by co-executors Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn to accept service of probate documents in USVI Superior Court, as Indyke resided in Florida and Kahn in New York. Despite this role in the estate proceedings, Kellerhals was not named as a defendant in the USVI Attorney General’s lawsuit against the Epstein estate, which named ten Epstein-created entities as co-defendants alongside Indyke and Kahn. Neither Kellerhals nor Business Basics VI LLC faced legal action in connection with the $105 million settlement.
